prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / stylized-concept.
Task: Redraw the Social Brave King's leg detail design sheet, correcting a repeatedly overlong calf. This is a faithful detail extraction and reconstruction of the already approved robot, NOT a new robot or a redesign. Make a polished landscape mechanical concept sheet with TWO LARGE VIEWS: left a front three-quarter leg detail including a short section of the original upper thigh, knee drill, complete calf and armored boot; right the SAME leg from the outer side, at the SAME scale and matching knee/ankle/sole levels. Warm ivory background, beautifully controlled black ink contours, clean cel shading, orange/ivory/graphite materials as in references, restrained metal highlights. No text, no measurements, no arrows, no logo. Keep ample margins and show the entire feet and heels.

REFERENCE ROLES:
Reference 1, the complete approved robot, is the PRIMARY AUTHORITY for the installed leg's actual proportions, shapes, armor breaks, tread placement, knee drill orientation, ankle and foot. Study its lower half carefully and keep those legs rather than inventing a new system.
Reference 2 is the drill vehicle design: the SAME machines supply the legs. Keep the recognizable polygonal ivory track-pod armor, orange support castings, black linked treads, dark road wheels and ribbed metal drills. The vehicle has compact distinct crawler-pod groups, NOT a single giant railway of wheels.
Reference 3 is an authored PROPORTION CONSTRAINT diagram only. Its simple polygons are NOT finished design shapes. It corrects the fatal previous error: knee-to-ankle is roughly one armored boot length, with a compact calf, articulated ankle and wide deep boot. Use the detailed shape language of references 1 and 2, not the simple shape design of reference 3.

CRITICAL PROPORTION:
The previous sheet was wrong because the shin was extended into a long thin wheel ladder and the white armor repeated too many times. Do NOT recreate that. The silhouette must be powerful, compact below the knee, and have a broad load-bearing boot just like reference 1. Include upper thigh context so the leg is not a giant calf on a tiny foot. On a conceptual 1000-unit-high drawing area the hip/upper thigh begins near 120, the drill/knee axis near 380, ankle pivot near 700, foot sole near 850. These are layout constraints, not visible text. Knee-axis-to-ankle distance must be approximately ONE boot's toe-to-heel length, not two or three boot lengths. Do not elongate the leg to fill the canvas. Leave blank space instead.

PART SHAPES AND DIRECTION:
- Original ivory segmented upper thigh descends to the orange knee drill carrier.
- A large silver cone drill projects FORWARD from the knee, along the same forward direction as that leg's boot toe. In side view face the boot and drill to the LEFT. No down-pointing or sideways knee drill.
- Compact broad calf: separated angular ivory shin plate sections, orange brackets and black linked tread surfaces visible through their gaps, recognizably the same segmentation as the full body. Two main shin armor sections, plus the separate ankle/boot armor; do not stack three or four identical long shin plates.
- Both front tread surface AND rear returning tread surface must be present, wrapped coherently around the compact wheel system. Never lose the front tread; never hang loose detached belts at the sides. Approximately four prominent compact wheel centers along the calf side, not seven/eight/nine stacked road wheels. Keep the ivory faceted lateral cover pieces of the source vehicle, not an entirely exposed uniform ladder.
- A real visible dark mechanical ankle hinge separates the calf from the boot. No fused solid tank-shoe leg.
- Very broad chunky wedge-toed boot, ivory upper instep plates, orange toe accents and orange heel supports, graphite sole. Compact foot wheel cluster at ankle/heel. The wide boot and ankle/heel structure MUST match the approved full-body leg, with toes and heel both clearly visible.
- No new weapons, no extra drill, no extra appendages, no redesigned tank chassis. The two panels must depict one identical leg and agree on armor count, wheel locations, tread path, boot length and knee direction.
Prioritize exact source geometry, coherent structure and the correct short/stout calf-to-boot relationship over decorative details.
